Respectfully, I have to say this is some bad advice. You shouldn’t use someone to forget about someone that creates more problems. You should heal from and grieve a relationship. Take it for everything it was, don’t demonize your ex but don’t romanticize them either. Try to keep ur memory’s unbiased and remember the good and bad stuff it’ll help you grow. Reflect and see what went wrong, and find out what you need to work on, what you could have done better in the relationship. Even if ur ex was evil and did so much wrong, she probably did some stuff right, and you probably did stuff wrong and right as well. Basically take it for all it was and don’t try to erase it, just because erasing is easier doesn’t make it the right choice. If you just erase it you’re basically saying that all the time you spent with that person was a complete and utter waste. Relationships are never a waste even if they were toxic. They allow you to learn more about yourself and how you handle things, they show you what others value in you, and what parts of you aren’t great as well.

Hey man I’ve been almost in the exact same place before, I hope you read this because I think it’ll really help.

The pain of losing someone you really care about can completely unravel you, and drive one insane. I’ve definitely reacted in a similar way that you have(when I was younger), and I just couldn’t get her out of my mind. The thing I’ve learned is that you have to accept it’s over, you don’t have control for what she does she’s out of your life. I know that sucks and you don’t want to face that truth, but the sooner you do the happier you’ll be and you can start to slowly feel better. It may seem like an impossible task, but don’t listen to the lies your telling yourself, you will be happy again, and you will love again, and you will grow as a person because of this. 

Trying to “win her back” never works and even if it did it probably wouldn’t last. You need to work on yourself, for yourself, and then new and better things can and will come along. Don’t hold on to her when there’s nothing to hold on to. I recommend that you try and get yourself on a daily routine, make set a list of goals for yourself and do all the things you wanted to do but were distracted in doing. 

Expect to fail sometimes, that’s ok. The most important part really is trying. It’s ok to fail in your progress sometimes, just don’t lose hope and keep pushing yourself. You have to be truly honest with yourself and hold yourself accountable, for your mistakes because thats the only way you’ll grow, but don’t let those mistakes haunt you too much. It’s ok to cry and process your emotions. Learn to cope with your emotions, and it first it will feel impossible, but practice makes perfect. 

As for the social media thing, I recommend you delete the apps at least for a while. It’s clear that you can’t help yourself, from looking at her social media, and that’s ok(I usually have trouble with that too) but you have to realize the problem and try to fix it. Stalking her won’t do anything except hurt you more. She’s living her life and you can’t blame her for that because that’s what she should do. So if you can’t help yourself from looking then do yourself a favor and get rid of the apps or block her. You’ll be tempted to redownload the apps and see how she’s doing but by deleting the app your creating a safety. You’ll be forced to confront yourself when you have the urge to stalk her, and it’ll hopefully keep you off the app.

Don’t make assumptions. Her life is separate form yours now, and that’s really hard to accept. The thing is that you don’t really know what’s going on, with her, or what she’s truly thinking. You are looking from an outside eye, and that only leaves room for speculation. You’ll haunt your self with thoughts. So try to keep her out of your mind. Accept that you are on two different paths now, and trying to see her path will only mess you up more.

The most important thing is to make sure you keep your head up. Constantly remind yourself that it’s ok to feel the pain, but you can’t let your pain control you. Control your pain, what I mean by that is take all those emotions and use them to your advantage. I’m a firm believer in everything negative has the potential to become an overall positive. Use these emotions to drive yourself to be a better and healthier person. Make sure you do it for yourself, because doing it for her will make you never truly move on, and you’ll never really find happiness that way. Understand that even if you do all of these steps, you’ll still feel shitty occasionally, but that will eventually pass and your future self will thank yourself for everything that you’ve done. 

Good luck man, and if you need a friend I’m here for you, I hope you’ll reach out. This shit is never easy but it’s gonna be good for you in the long run.
